scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it was right or wrong for me to delete my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week at the beginning of the school year. My dad and his mom went on a trip to help her parents with something. I brought my Switch because my school is more than an hour away, and I wanted something to do during the train commute every day. My stepbrother wanted to play on it, and since he's really into it, it actually helped distract him while I studied. So, I made a new profile for him on my Switch so he wouldn't mess up my saves. When I got back to school, I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eShop. So, I just deleted his profile. Now, this early morning, I got on the train to go to my dad's for Thanksgiving. I usually go home to my mom's, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family, and I'm not up for going on a plane trip. Anyway, I brought my Switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago, my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it, he started crying. Not full-on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he's holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn't think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my Switch over when I visit. So, was it right or wrong for me to delete his profile? Let me think about this step by step. First, I made the profile for him to use while I was watching him. That was considerate because I didn't want him messing up my saves. It also helped distract him while I studied, which was helpful for both of us. However, when I got back to school, I got annoyed with having to switch profiles each time I used the Switch. That's understandable because it's an extra step, and it can be annoying. So, I decided to delete his profile to avoid that inconvenience. But then, when I brought the Switch over for Thanksgiving, my stepbrother wanted to play, and when he found out his profile was deleted, he got upset. He even cried a little, which shows how much it meant to him. My dad also thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knew my stepbrother was enjoying playing on it. So, was it right or wrong? On one hand, I was annoyed by the extra step of switching profiles, and I wanted to avoid that. On the other hand, deleting the profile without discussing it with my stepbrother or my dad was hurtful and caused emotional distress. I should have communicated with my stepbrother before deleting his profile. Maybe we could have found another solution, like setting up the profiles in a way that was less inconvenient for me but still allowed him to play. Or, if that wasn't possible, I could have talked to him about why I was considering deleting the profile and maybe come to a mutual agreement. By deleting the profile without discussing it, I caused unnecessary hurt and tension. It's important to consider other people's feelings, especially when it comes to shared items like the Switch. Even though I didn't think it was a big deal, it clearly was for my stepbrother and my dad. In the future, I should remember to communicate and find solutions that work for everyone involved, rather than making unilateral decisions that could hurt others.
